editor_summary: Sample briefing. In a typical run the editor opens with the one or two signals most likely to change spending plans, then notes what is still only worth watching.

signals.headline: Example: a new low-cost inference chip announcement
signals.summary: Illustrative sample entry, not a real event. A hypothetical startup claims lower cost per token than current GPUs on a common benchmark.
signals.why_it_matters: If buyers can serve the same models on cheaper silicon, GPU demand growth could slow.

signals.headline: Example: a distilled model that matches a larger one
signals.summary: Illustrative sample entry, not a real event. A hypothetical lab reports a small model reaching similar quality with far fewer parameters.
signals.why_it_matters: Fewer parameters per task usually means fewer GPU hours per customer.

signals.headline: Example: cautious capex commentary on an earnings call
signals.summary: Illustrative sample entry, not a real event. A hypothetical cloud provider says it will pace data center spending.
signals.why_it_matters: Direct demand signal if it becomes a trend across providers.
